I was shocked by my visit to dentist Nina Lionidovna Ovchinnikova. I've been to the clinic on Korzhovka many times, using free numbing as a multi-child mother to save on budget. The numbing had never failed me before, so I saw no point in paying extra. Now, I came to see Ovchinnikova with pain in my left lower 5th tooth, planning to fix the 7th one later. She started raising her voice at me, saying the 5th tooth was perfectly healthy and didn't need treatment, that she's been working for a long time and knows better than me. Meanwhile, she was poking at the 7th tooth, causing me pain, and asked if she should continue. I didn't argue, let her start with the 7th. Last time, they'd diagnosed a cavity in the 5th tooth, and it was hurting, but now it was supposedly healthy? She gave me a shot, waited, then started drilling. The pain was sharp and intense, the numbing didn't work at all. She raised her voice at me, saying it shouldn't hurt and I was an unreasonable patient. When I asked why she was being rude, she said I was the rude one. After another shot, the numbing finally worked. But Ovchinnikova said it couldn't have worked that fast. I must be faking it for fun. They cleaned the canals for a long time, doing an X-ray twice because they didn't clean it properly the first time. In the end, she told me the tooth couldn't be further treated and the pain would last from two days to two weeks. They made me sign something in my chart, and I was free to go. I don't know what I signed. I was on the verge of fainting. With such attitude, one shouldn't work with people. I also wondered if she deliberately harmed me, so the tooth would need to be removed later. Why should the pain last for two weeks if the nerve was removed?

I arrived by prior appointment with two small children: a 5-year-old boy and a 2.5-year-old girl. We needed to have photopломбы placed. We were scheduled for 13:00 and 14:00. Arriving at the clinic at 12:45, we were directed to the registration desk to fill out forms. The woman at the registration desk had a very important air about her and handed me two contracts, saying, "Fill these out." I learned from her that getting a card costs 600 rubles. I objected, saying that if it's paid, maybe she could fill it out herself, as I would dictate the information. She refused, saying she had more important work to do, although there was no one else around the registration desk. Previously, when my son's teeth were treated in other clinics, they never asked me to fill out anything, they did it all themselves quickly and efficiently, and I just signed and paid. Naturally, I refused to fill it out myself and called the specialist we were scheduled to see. It was already 13:00. The specialist, a woman with a pleasant voice, heard about my problem and said she would come down and sort it out. A minute later, I saw her, and she explained that I needed to pay 1200 rubles for the first consultation, not for the card. I replied that we didn't need a consultation, I had no objection to the card, but we just needed to have photopломбы placed. In response, she sternly declared that if I didn't want to consult and get a card, she couldn't take us, adding that it was our problem. In the end, she said, "Sort out your own problems" and left.
I thought that if we were scheduled with her at 13:00 and 14:00 and she treated us like this, there were probably another 20-25 people without an appointment waiting for her, so she didn't value her clients much.
After all this, I went home. Fortunately, there's another good clinic where the children have an appointment scheduled for the day after this one.

I'm utterly shocked by today's visit to the pediatrician, Sokolova (our regular pediatrician is on vacation, she's substituting). She was rude to me from the moment I stepped in, even before I entered the office. "Who are you?" she asked, "And where's your card?" It's a strange question since this wonderful clinic doesn't give out cards. She sat there staring at her computer for 10 minutes, I was waiting, my grandmother went to the registrar to find out about the card's fate. Then they brought the card and the doctor deigned to ask why we were there. After hearing that another pediatrician heard heart murmurs in the child, she asked a brilliant question: "So, what do you want me to do, listen to it?" I replied that it would be nice. She didn't listen, just gave a referral to the cardiologist (forgetting to mention that he won't be there for 1.5 months). Her tone and manner of speaking scared the child (she was rude, to put it mildly). Looking at the child, who was about to cry, she said, "Well, do something, you're raising him." I wanted to ask what she's doing there, getting a salary from the money that people pay in taxes. And another question to the administration: why hasn't the issue of how cards get to the doctors been resolved for at least 1.5 years? If you don't give out cards, create a system that works and not every second person who comes in has to run between the office and the registrar looking for their card.

A heavy-duty hospital patient needed a medication that couldn't be bought anywhere in St. Petersburg on Friday. The price was 28,000 rubles and above. It was ordered through wer.ru. Delivery was from Moscow on Tuesday. Until Tuesday, 9 tablets were borrowed from another patient with a promise to return them on Tuesday morning. Also, a car was ordered for Tuesday morning to transport the patient for treatment 250 km away from St. Petersburg.
To cut the story short, the medication wasn't delivered.
It started with a call from the courier around noon, who indifferently informed us that our medication had been delivered to another city resident by mistake, the package was opened, she was too far away and had no time, and it wasn't her responsibility anyway. Then the pharmacy called, unable to understand that they were talking about the health and treatment of a heavy-duty patient, that the medication was vital, and asked us to wait until tomorrow. What "tomorrow" are they talking about when the medication needs to be taken "yesterday"?! They said the courier was on the other end of the city (this was still before lunch!), couldn't come to us, and suggested I leave my work and patients and go myself to meet the courier on the other end of the city.
You know, I've never encountered such irresponsible, indifferent attitude towards people - whether it's the courier service or the pharmacy itself, I don't care. I care about the patient's health and treatment.
Many hours were spent on phone calls - to no avail.
In the end, we had to turn to the internet again and look for the medication from other suppliers. We succeeded! And we were helped by very responsible employees of another pharmacy on Borovaya - the pharmacy manager himself delivered the medication to the patient that same day. Big thanks to them!
But I wouldn't recommend using wer.ru again - they'll let you down! There are many similar negative reviews.

We ended up at this clinic with our son last year (2014). The money-making scheme started even over the phone when making an appointment: I asked to schedule an appointment with a pediatric dentist, and since the earliest available slot was two weeks away, the girl on the phone suggested scheduling with a hygienist, saying that she also performs treatments. I was skeptical, but we scheduled an appointment anyway as we needed to address the tooth issue urgently.
On the appointed day, the doctor herself said that she doesn't handle treatments and that I must have misunderstood the receptionist. Nevertheless, she agreed to examine and clean the teeth. The hygienist (whose name I don't remember, but her first name was Ella) left a positive impression, despite a few attempts to overcharge us.
While our child was in the chair, the future dentist, Matveeva E., entered the room. The hygienist praised our child's behavior, but Matveeva seemed disinterested, with a blank stare and the thought "how annoying you all are" written on her forehead. I attributed this to her being busy with another patient. However, when we went for our appointment with Matveeva, the same thing happened. She treated our child like a non-entity and answered my questions condescendingly, as if she had just transferred from a public clinic to a private one and hadn't adjusted yet. In the end, we decided not to have her treat our child's teeth. To top it off, we heard a male doctor in the neighboring room raising his voice and a child crying (the child was alone in the room). After that, we vowed never to return to Zubrenka.
And yes, for such high fees, we could get better service at the local clinic, where they would lick our hands and shower our child with care and attention. In the end, we returned to the local clinic for our dental needs.

aspect_term: neurologists L.L. Goloborodko and O.R. Kuznetsova
english_translated:
I want to leave a negative review about the neurologists L.L. Goloborodko and O.R. Kuznetsova.

Their negligence and indifference almost led to serious health problems for me.
I'll start by saying that in March 2013, I went to Goloborodko L.L. with severe back pain. The doctor examined me, administered a block, injected painkillers, ordered an X-ray, and prescribed: milgamma, dip rylif, painkillers, etc. After that, thankfully, my back pain subsided, and I started swimming and doing special exercises. However, in September 2014 (after 1.5 years), I again went to Goloborodko with severe back pain. The doctor followed the same scheme, adding physiotherapy and ksefokam injections, which I faithfully attended, but they were ineffective.

The next time, I decided not to go to L.L. but to make an appointment with O.R. Kuznetsov (who was highly praised). Yes, the doctor conducted a more thorough examination of my spine (also looked at the X-ray results), and said: you have a very strong spinal curvature. I'm canceling the physiotherapy, canceling the ksefokam prescribed by Goloborodko, as it's ineffective in your case. Swimming also turns out to be harmful, according to him (despite the fact that swimming is generally recommended for spinal problems). Meanwhile, I paid more than 1000 rubles for the ksefokam prescribed by L.L.

It's great: one doctor experiments and prescribes, the other experiments and cancels, and the patient suffers both physically and financially!

Moreover, when I went to O.R. Kuznetsov, I said that I hadn't found any relief from L.L.'s treatment: my back continued to hurt despite the medication, injections, physiotherapy, etc. And I'm only 30! Neither of the mentioned doctors thought to prescribe an MRI!

Of course, I went to another clinic, where they immediately prescribed an MRI, which was approved by my insurance without any questions. The MRI showed multiple Schmorl's nodes in the thoracic spine. And I was prescribed a completely different, appropriate treatment, which actually helped me feel better.

After visiting these "doctors," I don't want to go to this clinic again, despite believing that there are also good doctors there.

On 06.10.2015, I visited the FGBU Polyklinika No.1 of the Russian Academy of Sciences (101000, Moscow, Sretenka Boulevard, 6/1, Sretenka Boulevard metro station) to see an ENT doctor, whose exact name I don't know (possibly Simkina Natalia Valentinovna), who was taking patients in room 307.

Firstly, not only is there no electronic queue, but there's also no possibility to schedule appointments. It's just a live queue with elderly people and the ensuing consequences: "I was here first", "I've already been here", "I just want to ask".

When I went to room 307, there was only one patient being seen, and no one else was waiting for an appointment in that room. I ended up waiting by the door for more than an hour. After examining my left ear, the doctor said it was clean and there were no foreign bodies. The examination took only 3 minutes.

When I asked for a more thorough examination, I was met with rudeness from this doctor. After taking my chart, I went to the registration desk and demanded the complaint book. The staff tried to resolve the issue and sent me to the 5th floor to see the hospital director, but he wasn't there.

Upon returning, I insisted on getting the complaint book, but they said they didn't know where it was because this situation was unprecedented. They promised to look into it.

Meanwhile, at the registration desk, they sent me to see another ENT doctor, Oleynik Pavel Anatolyevich, in room 309 without waiting in line. After listening to his disapproving comments about my behavior, he examined me.

His conclusion was similar: the eardrum was clean. There was a 3 mm traumatic erosion on the lower wall of the left external auditory canal. That's all!

Today, 07.10.2015, I went to another clinic. The ENT doctor there found a foreign body (a hair) in my left ear, removed it, and cleaned the ear. I'm very grateful to her.

My conclusion: the ENT staff there is incompetent and rude. I'll never go back there, even if they introduce electronic queues or scheduling.

On October 26, 2013, I checked my vision with Dr. Kapunova and bought glasses at the "Linsmaster" salon located in the "Our" shopping center (Solntsevo). I bought glasses for distance vision, with a 2-week warranty. I've been wearing glasses since 2000. On October 22, 2013, I checked my vision at the city clinic (-2 and -1.5), and they gave me a prescription for -1.5 and -1.25. Before buying glasses, I decided to make sure I had the correct prescription from our district doctors and went to the salon for a vision check and further purchase, which is located in my district. The vision check was quite quick (-2 and -1.5), which surprised me, as I didn't receive any advice on the correct frame or lens selection. I ignored the difference from the clinic's prescription, as I believed that large networks of famous brands employ highly qualified specialists, and the diagnosis at Linsmaster costs 500 rubles. They wrote a prescription for -1.5 and -1.0. They started offering anti-scratch lenses, as they didn't have regular ones, and I would have to wait a long time (I didn't ask how long). They quickly offered anti-scratch lenses for an additional 1100 rubles, which I agreed to, as the price was reasonable considering my inexpensive frame. The glasses cost 2999 rubles. After wearing them for a week (from October 26 to November 2), my right eye (dominant) was watery, I had headaches, and I felt discomfort. I doubted the correctness of the lens selection and vision check. On November 2, 2013, I went to a familiar person (whom I found only on October 31) to check my vision again, for the third time, to see if it was correct or not. They checked my vision and gave me a prescription for -1.5 and -1.25. When I returned to this salon, they refunded everything according to the warranty, but they spoke a lot about how this couldn't happen, that I wasn't used to wearing glasses (I guess I should get used to them over years, losing even more vision from such diagnosis). They only refunded the money for the frame and lenses, and they don't have a program for incorrect diagnosis, as the employee of Linsmaster told me. After this experience, I was very happy to have a familiar person who can correctly diagnose vision and select lenses. This is my story related to Linsmaster. Please consider it and make your conclusions.

The vision check was quite quick (-2 and -1.5), which surprised me, as I didn't receive any advice on the correct frame or lens selection. I ignored the difference from the clinic's prescription, as I believed that large networks of famous brands employ highly qualified specialists, and the diagnosis at Linsmaster costs 500 rubles. They wrote a prescription for -1.5 and -1.0. They started offering anti-scratch lenses, as they didn't have regular ones, and I would have to wait a long time (I didn't ask how long). They quickly offered anti-scratch lenses for an additional 1100 rubles, which I agreed to, as the price was reasonable considering my inexpensive frame. The glasses cost 2999 rubles. After wearing them for a week (from October 26 to November 2), my right eye (dominant) was watery, I had headaches, and I felt discomfort. I doubted the correctness of the lens selection and vision check. On November 2, 2013, I went to a familiar person (whom I found only on October 31) to check my vision again, for the third time, to see if it was correct or not. They checked my vision and gave me a prescription for -1.5 and -1.25. When I returned to this salon, they refunded everything according to the warranty, but they spoke a lot about how this couldn't happen, that I wasn't used to wearing glasses (I guess I should get used to them over years, losing even more vision from such diagnosis). They only refunded the money for the frame and lenses, and they don't have a program for incorrect diagnosis, as the employee of Linsmaster told me. After this experience, I was very happy to have a familiar person who can correctly diagnose vision and select lenses. This is my story related to Linsmaster. Please consider it and make your conclusions.

I want to share my impression of the "Predtecha" medical center, particularly my opinion of my treating doctor, Korchma Lyudmila Ivanovna. When I came to the center in early November 2010, I was pleased by the hospitality and friendliness of the staff. Initially, I underwent diagnostics with Ogulov A.T., who appointed Korchma Lyudmila Ivanovna as my treating doctor, saying that I needed to normalize my condition. As it turned out later, only 2-3, maximum 4 sessions were needed. After the initial examination, I had my first session, which I liked very much (55 minutes). Lyudmila Ivanovna briefly explained what she was doing and why. However, my subsequent visits left me increasingly disappointed (I had four sessions):
Firstly, the treatment session lasted only 40 minutes, although I was told it would be at least an hour, and that's what the website's price list states (1 hour - 1 hour 15 minutes). It seemed that Lyudmila Ivanovna didn't know what else to do... and she didn't explain what she was doing. Most of the time was spent on vacuum deep tissue therapy, which is half the price (not a manual massage by the doctor). Paying 2300 rubles per session (not a small amount!), I expected quality treatment!
During one of the sessions, Korchma Lyudmila Ivanovna said I would need at least 10 sessions, although on the third session, I felt that everything was fine, and she herself said that everything was in order! Therefore, further visits to the "Predtecha" medical center were not necessary. Lyudmila Ivanovna still scheduled more sessions for me... Moreover, she actively promoted the products of the "Predtecha" LC (not disputing their quality), immediately adding them to my receipt without asking if I would buy them or if I had the money for them at that moment. Her attitude towards the patient, as a treating doctor who should behave appropriately, was shocking: she didn't engage in dialogue, explain the treatment and methods used, or what the patient should and shouldn't do in their daily life to improve their condition.
Lyudmila Ivanovna said, "Come in - we'll fix everything...". Such an attitude was very unpleasant (it was clear: "Come more often and pay more!"). I won't go into other details of our brief communication. The last time I went to her for a consultation (after Hemoscan) with the diagnostic results, I wanted her to explain the results and the upcoming treatment - antiparasitic, as the woman who did the diagnostics said that the treating doctor would provide more detailed information about the diagnostics and treatment! And what happened? I was 5 minutes late for valid reasons, and I had to wait for Lyudmila Ivanovna for 30 minutes! She was seeing another patient. Why have a schedule if she can just take another patient without calling, warning, or asking if I would even come or the reason for my delay? Not to mention that my entire further schedule was disrupted (everyone is busy, and it's important to value everyone's time). She received me as follows: she briefly looked at the results, wrote down 2 medications on a sheet of paper, and gave it to me. She didn't explain anything about the parasites, how they act, what would happen if they develop, about the treatment itself, the action of these medications, their composition, etc. - in short, she didn't provide any information that a treating doctor should provide. I had to ask her to repeat the name of one of the medications, as she wrote it down silently without commenting on what and how much to take. In short, I was with her for no more than 5 minutes, but "the main thing" - she didn't forget to issue a receipt for the consultation (what consultation?) for an amount greater than the price list! If I hadn't looked at the price list, I would have overpaid! When I asked how long the consultation would last, Lyudmila Ivanovna answered - "It doesn't matter if it's 5 minutes or an hour, the price is the same!". You can imagine what kind of consultation that is for 5 minutes! I asked her how many sessions would be needed depending on the severity of the disease. Lyudmila Ivanovna's response shocked me, as in my opinion, a qualified doctor would never think of such a thing. "Regardless of whether a person is sick or not, whether they need treatment or not, they need 10 sessions or more". Lyudmila Ivanovna's attitude spoiled my overall impression of the "Predtecha" center. I think appropriate measures should be taken. With such an attitude towards her work, she is undermining the reputation of the medical center!

Everyone, be healthy!

I want to give my assessment of the Clinic on Leninsky Prospekt and about the surgeon, Klimenko Konstantin Vladimirovich. Perhaps this will help those who are thinking about where to go and where it is better to have an operation. I stumbled upon this clinic on the internet and immediately got the impression that everything is fast, high-quality, and beautiful. Thinking this way, I made an appointment and ended up with this surgeon. During the appointment, he looked at me and said that after the operation, I could go home immediately and full healing would take 20-25 days. When I told him that the recovery periods of others are significantly longer and that not everyone stitches the wound completely, but looks at the resected area, I heard the answer that they are all incompetent (idiots) and don't understand anything about this. This should have probably raised an alarm, but I really wanted to get rid of this problem as soon as possible and scheduled the operation. I came at the appointed time and it turned out that another operation was scheduled for my time, although I think that by paying a considerable amount of money, you should get appropriate treatment. Moreover, they took a young man who came to them in the morning, they fed him with promises all morning that he would lie down soon, but he only lay down at the appointed time for me at 18:00. I had to wait in the ward for an additional two hours. During the operation, I asked again about the rehabilitation period. And a miracle happened! It turned out that the period had increased from 20 days to 2 months, and maybe more. It won't be possible to leave after the operation immediately, as written on the website, but you need to wait for 2-3 hours for the anesthesia to wear off. And forget about sitting in a car and driving. They let me go and said to come back in 3 days for a bandage change. At first, they called me and asked about my well-being and even came home once. But this was only until I paid the remaining amount. In fact, the amount written in the contract was less, the remaining amount the doctor took for himself. In principle, I don't mind this approach, if not for the attitude. After that, they simply forgot about me and no longer asked about the healing process. If I hadn't gone to the bandage change with Golovko Yevgeny Borisovich, I don't know how the healing would have gone. Because he found stitches that my surgeons didn't see, and we tried various ointments to speed up the processes. The operation was performed on March 7, and the full healing of the wound occurred on June 10. I want to say to everyone who is thinking about an operation with Klimenko, think and look for other surgeons. There are many of them, and this one should be avoided.

During the examination, the doctor immediately suggested using a hormonal ointment. Despite my explanation that we had already tried this medication without success, I received no response other than confused comments like "all doctors prescribe this." The medication was not related to the reason for our visit. The doctor then looked at me and asked if we would be getting tests done, without providing any suggestions about the current situation. She offered no comments on whether the tests were necessary or not. After that, we returned to the waiting room, where the doctor advised us to wash the girl with chamomile until the test results were ready, which would take another 3 days (despite the fact that we had come in with urgent inflammatory discharge). She said she couldn't do anything else to help. When I asked about alternative options, she didn't respond, and when I asked how to find out the test results, she directed me to the registration desk. In the end, we paid 1,700 rubles for the doctor's advice to use chamomile and wait for her equally qualified opinion (which we probably paid another 1,700 rubles for). I never write reviews, but in this case, the doctor's complete lack of knowledge and apathy is truly shocking. Please, hire at least pediatricians of a decent level.

We ended up there. In short, I'll start from the beginning, or rather, from the threshold. We came to inquire about which specialist to go to - my husband's back (lumbar region) hurts (prices vary for everyone, I can't remember exactly, but roughly - neurologist 900, manual therapist 1500, osteopath 3500). The administrator (probably the main one who scams) told us, you can go first to the neurologist, find out which specialist you need, but you'll pay like this - 900 + 1500 (if a consultation is needed) + 3500, so we decided, since the osteopath is also a neurologist, we'll go straight to him (appointment 3500).

Our mistake was that we didn't get an MRI done beforehand, but we asked the administrator and the doctor, do you accept without a scan? And still, maybe it's better for us to get a tomography done first and then come back to you? To which the administrator said - the doctor will tell you, and the doctor just said - we'll see (you know, you've got to make some money 3500 for the appointment).

They led my husband behind a screen (of course, for such a price that the osteopath charges, you could make a nicer cabinet and interior!), and in one cabin, several people are taken at once, someone is getting a massage, someone is with the manual therapist (it reminds me of a Soviet-era physical therapy clinic), well, the doctor twisted my husband this way and that, and then said, you had an injury at 10 (my husband is 30), you fell hard on your butt and your coccyx got dislocated and the tissues got twisted, that's why it hurts now. Well, I already found it funny, honestly, how he could determine an injury from 10 years ago. My husband couldn't remember any serious injuries, he asked his mom, she also said there were no serious injuries. Well, he fell like all children do and that's it.

IN SHORT, then he supposedly (!) put the coccyx back in place and removed the pain (but the pain didn't go away).

Saying that the pain didn't go away and it didn't even get a little better, he said, you still need to get it adjusted, come back next time. My husband came back. Another 3500 rubles, he adjusted it again. Well, it didn't get any better after the appointment (why, I wonder, and for what they took the money), in the end, the osteopath says - then I don't know what's wrong with you. You need to get a tomography done and come back to us!

After that, we didn't really want to go back.

We got a tomography done, it turned out to be herniated discs and spinal canal stenosis. I wanted to go demand my money back, but there's no one to leave the child with, but we won't be going back there.

I want to share my story with you. My dad was sent to this research institute with joint problems. The referral was given by the local clinic. After calling the registration desk, I found out that they don't accept such referrals anymore, only through the Ministry of Health, and that the referral is only for a consultation. So, I went to the Ministry of Health, waited for 3 hours, and finally got the desired referral (thank you very much for the promptness). Full of hope that my dad's suffering would finally end and he would be cured, I called the registration desk of the Institute of Rheumatology, and received a wonderful response: they only accept Ministry of Health referrals for hospitalization, and consultations are paid (pay attention to the full name of this institution: Federal State Budgetary Institution "Scientific Research Institute of Rheumatology" of the Russian Academy of Medical Sciences). Further, in confusion, I asked how this could be, since the registration desk had said just a week ago that consultations were also through the Ministry of Health, and I was told: you were simply told incorrectly. I asked for the chief doctor's phone number, they directed me to the information desk (before calling the registration desk, I tried to call the information desk for 30 minutes, but it was either busy or they didn't pick up). I tried to explain to the registrar that the information desk wasn't answering. I asked again for the chief doctor's phone number, they refused. I asked for her surname, she hung up, and for the next 15 minutes (I didn't call again after that), they didn't pick up. I can't say anything about the doctors yet, as we haven't had an appointment yet, but I want to say one thing: before taking any action, it's better to call not the registrars, but the chief doctor who signed their orders when they were hired. Because they won't just not help, they'll also misinform you. It's good that there's someone to go for dad, but imagine how many elderly people come on their own with crutches and end up with nothing because of such employees who work in this registration desk.

I have a serious illness that causes bone destruction, including vertebrae. Four vertebrae were in critical condition since last year. I had vertebroplasty (filling with special cement) done on two of them in December 2014 at MONIKI, and I had to wait for hospitalization to strengthen the next two. The wait was very long, leading to almost complete destruction of one of the vertebrae and severe pain. Even strong painkillers didn't help. In June, I learned that the Medical Center on Dzerzhinsky Street had purchased the necessary equipment for such operations, and I turned to S.S. Kupov, the chief physician of the medical center, who specializes in these operations. After reviewing my MRI and CT scans, Sergei Sergeevich concluded that simple vertebroplasty would not be enough to strengthen my destroyed vertebra, as its walls could not withstand the pressure of the cement. Then Sergei Sergeevich took responsibility for finding possible solutions to my problem. A solution was found, and in July, I had a successful operation. They literally saved my life. I also want to note the high level of technical equipment in the operating room and the quality of the operations. I am grateful to all the center's staff for their professional service, friendly atmosphere, and attentive attitude towards clients. Special thanks to R.R. Borsukh, with whom I have been consulting and treating for about three years. I was referred to him by friends and now also recommend him as a highly qualified doctor. And a special HUGE THANK YOU to Sergei Sergeevich Kupov, whose merits as the chief physician and a specialist doctor are immeasurable: all his knowledge, activity, initiative, energy, etc., are directed towards the firm intention to help people and, undoubtedly, at a high level. I wish the Center prosperity!

Office No. 25. 07.08.2013. Certificate signed by:
Office Manager - Nikolaeva N.G.
Diagnosis - Spinal Arthritis.
Result - No group assigned.
Hospital documents and records, including those from the Institute of Rheumatology, were provided. At the time of application, inflammation was present in the cervical, left shoulder, left clavicle, right elbow, lumbar, knee, and ankle joints, as well as in the toes.

Before applying, to get there, I took 100 mg of Diclofenac (instead of the morning's 50), spent most of the previous day in bed. As a result, I was quite mobile (not counting limping, abdominal pain (due to tablets) and a sharp limitation in speed of movement.
Which, as it turned out, worked against me. For the main argument for refusal was this very mobility of mine.
The additional comment was: "But you don't have any swollen or hot major joints!" Apparently, the ankle and clavicle joints are not large enough (and the degree of joint swelling depends directly on the amount of movement and the dose of medication). As for the temperature, even during periods when various joints were just being affected by the disease and had sizes significantly exceeding the norm (and very strong pain, of course), the temperature on them did not rise significantly. Apparently, this possibility was not known to the doctor "with a 30-year experience". The difference in mobility was also "not noticed".
No one paid attention to the dactylitis of the toes. And this, despite the fact that it is they who react the strongest, ensuring strong pain after an hour or two not in a lying position, i.e. preventing walking. They also do not allow wearing normal shoes, condemning to things 3-4 sizes larger, no hard surfaces!
I was unable to prove that the body reacts with pain and temperature to several hours out of bed. I asked the commission - they also don't know how to do it.
The data of biochemistry and blood analysis also said nothing about inflammation (ESR 3 times higher than normal, CRP - 7).
Now I'm lying with a temperature of 38, unable to walk without crutches and for 5 meters due to pain, and thinking, what would be the argument for assigning a group in my case?

On March 18, 2013, I gave birth to a son at the 20th maternity hospital. Everything went smoothly. However, I was sent home at 8 am after my mucus plug had released, as the doctor, Salikhova, said it was only the precursors of labor and my cervix was only dilated 1 cm. But by evening, the pains had intensified and became more frequent, so at 11 pm, my husband and I went back to the hospital.
This time, Dr. Khavantsov B.V. was on duty, he immediately sent me to the delivery room as I was 2-3 cm dilated. He then ruptured my membranes to speed up the process. He asked about my mindset for the delivery, I said I was very positive and calm, and he agreed that a positive attitude is crucial. He performed everything professionally. I wanted anesthesia, and Dr. Khavantsov explained its pros and cons. I was under anesthesia for the last 3 hours, so the delivery left only pleasant memories. The anesthesiologist, a man, was excellent, I don't know his last name, but he worked quickly. The relief after contractions without anesthesia was immense!
The midwife who delivered me was Badenkina N.A. I am incredibly grateful to her! She supported me, guided me on how to push and breathe. She is a wonderful, kind person and an excellent midwife. In short, my gratitude knows no bounds. The baby was born very easily, with just 3-4 pushes. I tore a little, but the cut was small, external, and healed quickly.
In the postpartum ward, I was placed in a single room, which was like a free VIP. The facilities were great, with a shower, toilet, and refrigerator. The doctor, Shilina I.L., also helped a lot after the delivery, explaining how to feed and express milk.
In conclusion, I want to thank all the staff of the 20th maternity hospital. To the expectant mothers, I want to say that childbirth is indeed associated with pain and emotions, so those who write that no one helped them, that they were shouted at, should initially set their mindset to positive. Then everything will be fine.

On May 27, 2011, I gave birth to a son! We arrived at the hospital with contractions every 5-7 minutes at 3:30 AM (my water broke in the morning of the 26th, and contractions started after a warm shower in the evening). There was no one else in the reception area, they did an ultrasound and examined me. The examining doctor was rude, but he was quickly put in his place. Then they gave me an enema and sent me to the delivery room. They did another ultrasound, attached a monitor, left me with "papaverin" suppositories that didn't help, and I asked for anesthesia, but it was too early as my dilation was small. An midwife stayed with me, teaching me how to breathe, talking to me, and giving me a ball that helped ease the contractions. Doctors kept coming in to examine me, around 11 AM they ruptured my membranes when I was completely exhausted and wanted to sleep. They decided to do an epidural, saying I could rest a bit. But as soon as they gave it to me, I relaxed and the process sped up. Within 10 minutes, I pushed once and gave birth! They didn't separate me from my baby, putting him on my stomach right away, and took us to the postpartum room together. They brought food almost immediately and checked that I went to the bathroom. I gave birth at 2:05 PM, and by 6 PM I was already walking around. Every day, doctors examined both me and the baby, teaching us how to care for him. The food was generally good, but there were products I couldn't eat as a breastfeeding mother. My relatives brought me everything, especially dairy products (which are necessary after birth to regulate digestion). Overall, I was very satisfied!

After enthusiastic online reviews of Maternity Hospital No. 20, we decided with my wife to give birth there, even for free. Being Moscow residents, we registered my wife at the women's clinic attached to the 20th maternity hospital. The doctor weighed us, listened to our pulse, and sent us for tests, which turned out to be countless. We dutifully submitted them all and waited for the birth. A month passed. My wife's due date seemed to have arrived, so we went to the maternity hospital, where we were immediately turned away by a certain "Olga Vladimirovna": there's no labor activity in you, and your tests have expired, HIV, AIDS, syphilis ended two days ago, and without them we won't take you, the hospital is "clean", we don't take pathologies. We were surprised, where was our pathology if all the tests were fine, ultrasound and CTG were in excellent condition? But the doctor was categorical, and we went to retake the tests. Getting the results, we went back to the maternity hospital, where we were again met by "Olga Vladimirovna". With obvious displeasure, she accepted our tests, but still sharply rebuked us - there are no places, sit and wait. The news that we already had 41 weeks and it was time for us to give birth was unexpected and unpleasant for her, apparently, she could no longer refuse us for some medical reasons and left us waiting in the reception room for three hours. That's when we started thinking that free births in our time are almost like an anachronism, and no one will welcome us with open arms.
My wife was eventually accepted, but sent to "pathology" because her labor hadn't started. She mentioned a "cesarean", but was strictly refused - no indications. And then it began: she lay in the ward for half a day waiting for any doctor, but no one came. Then, the next day, a catheter was inserted into her cervix, supposedly "for gel application". It's impossible to ask for a pill or injection for pain relief - you're not allowed, endure it. The next two days, the doctors played hide and seek - they appeared rarely and mostly remained silent. At night, my wife's contractions started, instead of the labor ward, she was sent to the nurse who gave her sedatives and an injection. After the continuing contractions, she was finally sent to the labor ward, placed on a chair, and they left. A drip was put in and forgotten for three hours. After persistent cries, a nurse finally came, put on a CTG, and forgot again, resulting in a meter-long cardiogram and great surprise from the doctor who came later. My wife mentioned a "cesarean" again. The answer was the same - no indications. My wife, of course, fell asleep again right there on the chair from the tranquilizers. At noon, she was woken up by surprised doctors from the next shift - let's go for a "cesarean". For this, a separate thank you to the doctor who understood that it was dangerous to delay the birth any further. That is, after three days of doing nothing to help my wife give birth, they finally took her for surgery. Everything went well - the baby was taken out, shown, and taken away. My wife was sent to the ward.
And then the most interesting part began - in the large, beautiful wards, the "paying girls" lie happily, with their own doctor attached and a nurse running at the first call. My wife has the most ordinary "Soviet" ward, a duty doctor comes occasionally, and rude nurses. Want water? Go get it yourself - after surgery! Want extra food? Wait, we'll bring a 50-gram bottle in the evening. And so on, there's milk, there's no milk - feed as you can. My wife had her first birth, she asked to be taught how to feed. The answer was - if there are problems, come as you like. On the fifth day, she was discharged with great pleasure, and it seems they were waiting for new paying patients. We, Moscow residents, find this sad and unpleasant. We can only watch as guests from the former Soviet southern republics come to give birth to their numerous offspring, and the doctors and nurses are happy to "lick" them.

My cousin was admitted to the hospital with acute chronic cholecystitis in the 2nd surgery department. He lived alone and upon admission said he had no close relatives. An operation was performed. They initially planned to do a laparoscopy but ended up doing an open surgery. The doctors were surprised when relatives arrived. After the operation, he felt well and his condition was improving. Then they inserted a dilator into his channel and that's when things started to go wrong. On the weekend, I visited him with a relative and was shocked by his condition. He was constantly vomiting, and IV drips were not helping. The on-call doctor didn't go into details, just looked at the vomit and changed the IV drip. They asked the nurses and orderlies to keep an eye on him overnight, of course, not for free. His ex-wife flew in from abroad. A strong, healthy man was wasting away before our eyes. The doctors said he needed to walk, but he couldn't get out of bed. He was vomiting and had severe diarrhea several times a day. His ex-wife begged the doctors, "Please get him on his feet. We'll reward you. Just cure him!" He was transferred to the ICU. They found two more ulcers in his duodenum. When talking to the doctors in the ICU, they said, "He was already very advanced, there's an inflammatory process. We're doing everything we can. There's no need to come here." In short, after 10 days in the ICU, he died. They found pneumonia. It turned out he was on a ventilator. Another operation was performed, but he didn't make it. I didn't have to talk to the surgeon; he was in the operation. I spoke with the head of the department. He explained everything in medical terms that we didn't understand. But how could a healthy 65-year-old man, who had never been sick, with excellent health, die after a routine operation from which patients are usually discharged after a week? The diagnosis was an abscess of the omental bursa. You can write anything you want in a diagnosis. My opinion, and not only mine, is that there is not enough care for patients now as there was in Soviet times. Everything depends on money. Maybe if we had paid immediately, everything would have been different? I don't know. God is the judge for all of us.

opinion_term: still didn't give me a definite diagnosis
english_translated:
At 16, I was in this hospital with appendicitis, and I was just shocked. I'll skip the part where they sent me to all the doctors because they couldn't figure out what was wrong with me. They still didn't give me a definite diagnosis and sent me for surgery: "Well, there's fluid in the pelvis, we need to do a laparoscopy to determine it exactly." (For those who don't know, that's when they make a small cross incision under the navel, insert a tube, inflate the abdomen with oxygen, and crawl around with a camera. Those who've had it done will agree it's not the most pleasant thing.)
The nice nurses came to prepare me. They undressed me, explained what they were going to do, put me on a gurney, and wheeled me away.
I was terrified: my first time in a hospital and straight to surgery. I was crying non-stop. During the laparoscopy, despite the anesthesia, it hurt so much from the oxygen pressing on my ribs and lungs that I couldn't even breathe. I told the anesthesiologist and begged, "Could you give me some pain medication?" He replied, "I don't owe you anything. Your mom and dad do. Endure."
There he was, standing by the table with a scared, crying 16-year-old kid, and he's being rude with a smug face.
Anyway, after some time, they diagnosed me with appendicitis and gave me full anesthesia.
It was Thursday night into Friday. All of Friday, I couldn't get up, but then they told me I had to walk. And on the weekend, I went to the bathroom for the first time without help.
Administrators, do you have a cleaner on weekends?!
There's excrement on the floor, the toilets aren't flushing because they're clogged, there's bloody paper and bandages in the trash bin, and the smell is just awful! Sanitation, my god!
I understand that there's construction going on and more people than usual in the wing, but then you need twice as many cleaners! This is A SURGERY WING! People are getting cut open here, and sanitation conditions are the most important thing!
So, I went to the bathroom, tensing all my muscles, making sure not to touch the toilet seat. I almost levitated over it.
In short, it was a mess, fear, and horror.

I gave birth at the 67th maternity hospital in 2000, although I only needed a consultation, I had a cardiogram done in the 9th month, there was no time for consultation, and I was admitted to give birth. Some people say it's terrible, others say it's great, I experienced both. I was admitted two weeks in advance, I don't know the doctor, I saw her once a day before giving birth, and once after, but I had no strength to say anything. The treatment was limited to taking iron supplements and having my blood pressure measured, two interns were probably in charge, they showed care. I have the first negative blood group, blood was taken for antibodies two weeks in advance, but then they said the lab was overloaded, so they didn't take it again. I wasn't tortured, no heart examination was done, why I was admitted early is unclear. I didn't discuss the birth with the doctors, I gave birth for free. The birth itself was a nightmare, we both survived, probably thanks to the doctors, I'm very grateful to them. During the birth, there was a single, tight nuchal cord, the baby got stuck, the umbilical cord tightened, I couldn't feel the contractions, my lower abdomen, lower back, and the entire right side of my body seized up. The team that delivered me acted quickly, I tried to do everything they said, and they managed to pull the baby out without using forceps or causing oxygen deprivation. The first stage was over, then a trainee and someone from the internship team stitched me up, I said it hurts, but they said it can't be, they gave me anesthesia. They took me to the corridor, I felt really bad, a doctor passed by, noticed me, examined me, called the head of the maternity hospital, it turned out I had a uterine hemorrhage and a hematoma on the posterior wall, they sent me to the operating room, called the pros and saved me (I lay in the ICU for a bit) thanks to the doctors, although I still don't know their names. Now I'm waiting for my second, I went to the cardiologist for a consultation at the 67th, they asked me why I didn't have an echocardiogram done when I was with my first, it turns out I have a prolapse that I didn't know about and some other deviations. In general, I encountered both professionals and amateurs in turn, so where to give birth is up to you, there are amateurs everywhere, but the professionals at the 67th are good.

opinion_term: highest professionalism, responsibility, and caring attitude
english_translated: Thank you very much to the entire staff of the 2nd Surgical Endocrinology Department and personally to the head of the department, Pogosyan Gagik Eduardovich, for their highest professionalism, responsibility, and caring attitude towards people. Wonderful doctors, nurses, and orderlies. Each employee knows their job and performs it with full dedication, not just because they have to, but because it brings them joy (even something like changing and pouring out bedpans can bring joy, as you're doing something good and necessary at that moment!). Excellent conditions in the wards, sterile cleanliness, comfortable beds (especially noticeable after surgery) with remote control, plastic windows - no drafts, no stuffiness, everything works perfectly (lighting, plumbing, heating, outlets), no barracks-like atmosphere (visits are of course limited in time, and that's right, but if a visitor stays longer, no one rushes them out or scolds them for leaving a puddle of dirt on the floor with their slippers on - they'll just quietly wipe it up; in fact, during my week-long stay from February 5 to 12, 2014, I didn't hear a single rude word or remark, either towards me or anyone else), good food (some might not find it very tasty, but some people also like hamburgers, but that doesn't mean we should eat them), adapted to the mostly sedentary lifestyle of post-operative patients. Of course, even after a good review, no one would want to end up in the hospital, but if it does happen, to those who mainly fear rudeness, dirt, and incompetence, I want to say that none of this applies to the 70th Hospital, at least to the 2nd Endo.

Discharged without being fully treated, still having a fever and without follow-up tests! I'm 27 years old, spent two weeks in the hospital with chronic purulent-obstructive bronchitis! They didn't do a control X-ray, didn't finish the physiotherapy, instead of the prescribed 10 times, I only got 5 magnet sessions and 6 inhalations, instead of 10. And it's all for nothing because my attending physician, Guumina Olga Lioniovna, if she can even be called a doctor, was negligent, rude, did rounds whenever she felt like it, sometimes not even looking at me. She completely ignored me, saying she'd come back later but never did. She didn't even look at my X-ray with pneumonia, which is what I was brought to the hospital for by ambulance. Plus, she said I only needed 2 antibiotics, but gave me 4-5 and kept changing them, so the treatment was practically useless. I was just like a rabbit to her. Guumina O.L. also increased my nebuhaler inhalation from 3 times a day to 4 times, even though my temperature was constantly rising after lunch, sometimes up to 38.5. I later found out that you shouldn't inhale with a nebuhaler when you have a fever. Before discharge (on the day of discharge), they took blood from my vein for a biochemical and clinical blood test. I asked if I should wait for the results, and they said, "If you need them so badly, come back tomorrow for the results." And today, we're discharging you!

Caution! Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov. His professionalism is highly questionable. On August 23, 2014, my wife Svetlana underwent an osteosynthesis operation (a metal plate was installed). She had a closed comminuted fracture of the upper third of the tibia with displacement. She was discharged a week after the operation. My wife told me (she was conscious) how the operation went, including the use of an electric drill to drill holes in the bone for plate fixation. The drill fell on the floor and stopped working. They had to get another one. The instruments were not changed, after all, they are good as they are. During the removal of the sutures, the suture line opened up and was taped. They were discharged like that and told to apply green paint. Two weeks later, the tape was removed by themselves. A sore remained, which turned out to be necrosis. From the emergency room, where we were sent for further treatment, we were sent for a consultation to the 71st hospital where the construction was installed. The doctor said, "Let nature take its course." The question arises, why? Why first introduce infection in the form of golden staph, and then let nature take its course? My wife is very sociable, and every time we visited the emergency room, in line, we always met former patients of Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov from the 1st traumatology department of the 71st hospital. In conversations with former patients of Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov, it became clear that we are united by one thing - infection, that very notorious golden staph. Events continued to unfold, the plate became infected, the leg swelled up. A fistula opened up. People shied away from us, saying, "We'll have a hard time with you," when they found out that the plate was installed by Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov from the 71st hospital (probably, Valentin Nikolaevich Borovkov is quite well-known among his colleagues). As a result, as of January 21, 2015, an Ilizarov apparatus is installed, the leg is 3 cm shorter, and disability is looming. Our case is not an isolated one. In 2012, Yelena Aleksandrovna Isaeva, born in 1973, had a more vivid experience with pictures. (http://mitin-deputat.livejournal.com/846.html) I want to appeal to the management of the 71st hospital. Please, put your house in order with both staff and hospital-acquired infection. There are already many disabled people, why increase their number? Sincerely, Vladimir.

On January 15-16, 2012, my wife and I accidentally spilled technical gasoline in the kitchen, which caught fire from a cigarette. I burned my legs up to my knees, and my wife burned her feet. We were admitted to the hospital. The night doctor treated our wounds and put us in separate wards. The next morning, the attending physician said that we needed a dressing change every two days. When I asked what we should do with ourselves, they simply told us to lie down and that was it. I asked if we could lie at home under our mother's supervision and come for dressing changes every two days. They said it didn't matter, but they wouldn't let us go, so I wrote a statement that I had no claims and did what I wanted. The hospital was dirty, unsanitary, the toilet was terrible, it was scary to go in, and it was impossible to call a nurse, they were always busy. So, I wrote a statement and went home. A familiar nurse did the dressing changes. A few days later, my wife's foot swelled up, we called an ambulance and went back to the hospital. The doctor smirked, "So, you're back!" My wife lay in the hospital for a few more days, calling me every two hours to say that everything hurt, no one was coming, the doctor said - dressings. It was difficult for her to go to the toilet, and a roommate took her on a wheelchair. Every time they passed the nurses' post, one of them would always reproach her, "They're taking you, your legs aren't broken." My wife would say, "You don't help, that's why the roommate is taking me." On Thursday, January 19, 2012, in the morning, my wife couldn't get out of bed, she took a chair as support and went to the duty room. She asked four doctors for help, saying that her legs hurt, help her. The doctors sent her back to the ward, saying, "If you're not satisfied, discharge yourself." My wife asked the nurses for help, they said, "You're crazy, we're busy." Although all three were doing nothing and having a nice chat. In the end, one brought a bandage, threw it on the bedside table, and said, "Wrap it yourself." My wife lay all day looking at the ceiling, and no one came. Closer to the evening, the roommates left for the toilet, and one old woman was left. A "nurse" came and put an IV on the old woman, then she said to my wife, "You won't lie here," and attacked her with a syringe. My wife, despite the excruciating pain in her legs (out of fright), got up and knocked the syringe out of her hand, the nurse then grabbed a chair and swung it at my wife, which also fell out of her hand. They fell to the floor and started fighting. At this moment, in the doorway stood the nurses and the doctor, they were all egging her on, "Hit her." From the next room, a girl of the same nationality as the nurse came in and grabbed my wife by the hair. She fought her off and started calling 112. The police arrived quickly. My wife wrote three statements about the attack, in which the doctor was mentioned. The duty officer arrived and tore up all three statements, saying, "You're writing it wrong." The medical staff present at the event wrote their versions of what happened. The duty officer accepted the statements. After talking to the police, they told my wife, "You won't do anything, there are more of them." The head of the department, just in case, called the psychiatric hospital. When the tough guy from the psychiatric hospital asked why they had come, they told my wife, "We work for him (head of the department) and he's our friend, get ready, we're taking you away." The head of the department also told my wife that it was pointless to complain because she wouldn't prove anything because she was alone. In the end, my mother came and took her out of that madhouse. Now we're going to a private clinic and we'll be treated for a lot of money. After I recover, I'll write to all the authorities. If anyone knows how and where to turn quickly, help. PS: Don't go to this hospital - it's hell!

After the anesthesia wore off, Dad felt okay at first. In my naivety, I brought Dr. Azimov a bottle of good whiskey. (From the bottom of my heart). I handed him the bottle, and then Azimov shouted at the top of his voice: "What am I, a plumber, that you're giving me a bottle!" I was in shock. He shouted loudly, for the whole corridor to hear. After the operation, my father felt bad all the time, and then metastases started. I want to address Azimov. Of course, it's impossible to prove that you behaved like this, it's impossible to prove that you took the money (and this is a criminal offense). I didn't record it on my phone, I was thinking about Dad. But there is God, and God sees everything! And everyone in this life gets what they deserve! I don't hate you, Rustam (I did before). I know that you will get what you deserve in your life. I pity you. Maybe it would be better for you to learn to be a plumber.
Friends! I repeat that this is just our story. And this is just a cry from my soul. You make your own conclusions. I sincerely wish you health! Some doctors really need it!

My father was in the hospital under SOGAZ insurance, we were transferred from the Central Clinical Hospital with a terrifying diagnosis of brain cancer, an urgent operation was needed, at the end of December 2012.
Without money, no one will even approach you, and what's worse, they won't approach you even with money. My father had a neurosurgical operation, they removed the brain cancer tumor. The operation went very well, the surgeon, Miklashovich Eduard Richardovich, is a professional from God, the next day after the operation, they took my father out of intensive care, he was talking, completely lucid. But then, the New Year holidays came. And instead of improvement, my father almost died.
There was no one left in the hospital. They didn't give me the doctors' mobile phone numbers, I was sitting with my father alone, the nurses only came to give injections twice a day. No amount of money could make them work. Once, before leaving for the night, I left them a bottle of Italian champagne for 2000 rubles, good chocolate candies, and 1000 rubles in cash, so they would come to him at night, because after the operation, he had insomnia and nightmares. My father, always a strong and tough man, cried from fear like a child, they locked him in a stuffy room so he wouldn't disturb the nurses, and took away the nurse call button, hid it behind the bed, he couldn't reach it, I paid for a private room with a TV, but they were too lazy to even turn it on for him! And he lay there in the heat, in the dark, for hours without sleep, motionless, because he had paralysis on the entire right side! In short, out of the 4 on-duty nurses, 2 were normal, but two were just sadists. I did their job, sat with my father from 10 am to 10 pm, and drove home every day for 55 km (I live in Lyubertsy). So, when I wasn't there, they didn't even always change his diaper and feed him! Although I always left 500 rubles every evening before leaving, so they would look after him! In Moscow, this is a normal price for a caregiver, but in this hospital, the sisters don't consider money!
The doctors in the hospital are not much better. During the holidays, there were only 3 patients left on the floor, who were probably so heavy that they couldn't be discharged. The doctors DIDN'T COME THEMSELVES! I had to catch them for hours, drag them into the room. Despite the fact that I gave everyone money and expensive cognac before the operation, and then some more. And my father was a commercial patient, the insurance company paid huge sums for us. I encountered such a state of the patient for the first time, I'm not a doctor, I didn't know what to do with a bedridden patient. And no one told me how to take care of him. No one even advised me to do something urgently or hire a professional for money. Although, the LFK specialist and massage should have been provided to us for free by the insurance! But the massage was only after the New Year holidays, around January 10th, and the LFK specialist said he would only work for cash, because, you see, he doesn't get anything from the money that the insurance company pays by wire, it all goes to the administration. I tried to argue and say that I'm not an oligarch either, and that if the insurance is paying, then I'm not obliged to, but he was inflexible. I had to pay so he would put my father on his feet and teach him to walk again with paralysis in his leg.
But that was later, and at first, I watched my father's condition worsen every day. After a week of lying like that, he could barely talk, he was almost motionless. I ran around the floors, looking for the on-duty doctors, begging them to come, but they ignored me or came just for show. And only one kind doctor, unfortunately, I don't know his last name, with a Korean appearance, said that, actually, the patient should have been sitting on the bed from the 3rd day after the operation, taught me how to do it, fixing it with a chair, - and also taught me how to do various procedures to prevent lung stasis.
I did everything myself, it was very hard. Some nurses helped me change the dirty, wet sheets and diapers under my father, some wrinkled their noses in disgust and refused to help.
And most importantly, in the end, when the cancer diagnosis was officially confirmed (histology, biopsy) - according to the insurance contract, they were no longer supposed to pay for further treatment. And they discharged us from the hospital. A bedridden patient who could barely take a few steps down the corridor with the help of a specialist. I begged, pleaded not to discharge him, there should be some recovery, procedures, rehabilitation. I was ready to pay for further stay myself. But no, they threw us out. They didn't provide an ambulance or anything. I had to hire porters, they carried my father into the house on their hands because our house has 2 floors without an elevator.
You know, this is a terrible hospital, terrible treatment of patients. Even with money, you're not considered a person there.

I consulted with gynecologist Meshalkina with an already established frightening diagnosis, screening results, and ultrasound, with a referral for pregnancy termination due to multiple incompatible with life fetal pathologies at 14 weeks. She reassured me, saying, "We will help you, but we need to repeat all the tests here in our center, otherwise we cannot hospitalize you and start your medical record." I paid an additional 2000 for the ultrasound, then waited 1.5 hours in line to see quack and old brute MD Demidov. In his office, I was greeted by a group of 10 medical students and rude, disrespectful treatment with no sign of compassion or sympathy. He then rewrote all the diagnoses from the results of the research from another center, as he couldn't see anything on their outdated equipment, and he described all the defects and abnormalities of my poor child in detail, laughing and joking with the students. I endured it because I needed his conclusion to be hospitalized. After paying another 2500 and waiting another hour, I finally entered Meshalkina's office, but she said she didn't know where I had been and that her workday was over, and I had to wait for the next on-duty doctor. Doctor Siluyanova conducted an examination, although she couldn't establish a diagnosis this way, wrote in my medical record for a long time, and said that the abortion would cost 50-60 thousand rubles, but there's no guarantee they would accept me. She needs to convene a consultation, and the chief doctor has a scientific council, and I have to wait a few more hours until it's over. In the end, I spent from 8 am to 5 pm in this so-called hospital, paying for unnecessary tests, going through humiliation and stress, and received a refusal over the phone! This is fraud. People, be vigilant if you want to preserve your health and honestly earned money. I filed a complaint with the prosecutor's office.

**Wow, the head nurse!**

Hello, I want to share my emotions after staying at this hospital. I've never written a review before and haven't read them either, but I really wanted to do this. I've never encountered such treatment in our country.

I was admitted with my child to the 5th department with a diagnosis of lacunar angina, fever, etc. We were received warmly and treatment began, but my child refused to stay in the ward and I had to sit on a bench in the corridor near the head nurse's office, watching the department's work. Well, what can I say, at first glance, a fragile girl with a friendly smile, but she's quite tough, my child even gave her the nickname "Cinderella").

First, she writes something down, then she takes the child to the toilet on a stretcher, five minutes later she's holding the child in the ward while the mother runs to the toilet, ten minutes later she returns with a basket full of medicines, and all you can hear throughout the department is "Nastya", then from another end: "Where's our Nastya?" And she's already standing at the door, still with that smile - amazing speed! And despite all this, she finds time to ask what's wrong, she came up to us and said we're not supposed to be in the corridor, she asked if there's a conflict in the ward, if something happened, I explained why I couldn't stay, and Anastasia Valerievna, joked with my child, gave us masks, and my daughter went to the ward herself half an hour later.

Everyone says head nurses are mean, but I want to say that I've proven this wrong myself, here the head nurse works day and night shifts and still remains friendly and interested. A real person!

It's very hard to be in the hospital when you're a man and there are only women around, but when you feel that there are people who will ask, who will be interested, it becomes easier. Health to you and your loved ones, Kobleva Anastasia Valerievna.

And of course, to the head of the department Mitrofanova I.V. and doctor Shakarayan A.K. - competent people, it's nice to know that there are still doctors by the grace of God! You, nurses and orderlies - thank you! A wonderful team!

Thank you, the leader, for having such a humane staff!

Well, what can I say, at first glance, a fragile girl with a friendly smile, but she's quite tough, my child even gave her the nickname "Cinderella").

First, she writes something down, then she takes the child to the toilet on a stretcher, five minutes later she's holding the child in the ward while the mother runs to the toilet, ten minutes later she returns with a basket full of medicines, and all you can hear throughout the department is "Nastya", then from another end: "Where's our Nastya?" And she's already standing at the door, still with that smile - amazing speed! And despite all this, she finds time to ask what's wrong, she came up to us and said we're not supposed to be in the corridor, she asked if there's a conflict in the ward, if something happened, I explained why I couldn't stay, and Anastasia Valerievna, joked with my child, gave us masks, and my daughter went to the ward herself half an hour later.

Everyone says head nurses are mean, but I want to say that I've proven this wrong myself, here the head nurse works day and night shifts and still remains friendly and interested. A real person!

It's very hard to be in the hospital when you're a man and there are only women around, but when you feel that there are people who will ask, who will be interested, it becomes easier. Health to you and your loved ones, Kobleva Anastasia Valerievna.

And of course, to the head of the department Mitrofanova I.V. and doctor Shakarayan A.K. - competent people, it's nice to know that there are still doctors by the grace of God! You, nurses and orderlies - thank you! A wonderful team!

Thank you, the leader, for having such a humane staff!

I want to address Dmitry Anatolyevich. Hello! We have a problem, and it's not small in scale. First, about my family: I have two children, the first is a newborn infant with disabilities, the second is frequently ill. Once, I ended up in the pediatric Izmailovsky Hospital No. 3 in the boxed infectious department (September 15-22), it's been about two and a half months since then. Then I was hospitalized again with my first child in the same hospital in the gastroenterology department. We were there for nine days, and then I received a call on my mobile from the TB dispensary, saying that we had contact with a TB patient in September in the hospital in the boxed department with the service staff. It turned out that the contact was with a person who was distributing food. Now, all TB dispensaries are searching for about 1,500 children, not counting adults. The chief physician of this hospital (Zharkov) refuses to comment on anything, and the deputy for medical affairs refers to the polyclinic, saying that they are blowing up a scandal. But as far as I know, the dispensary does not come home if there is no cause for concern. Now, about what is happening in the hospitals: there should be wards for at least one mother with a child (not 4 mothers and 6 children in a box with different diseases). There should be a toilet and a bathroom, at least at the end of the corridor (mothers have a toilet in the basement, where water drips from the ceiling, and there are no baths, nor beds. Mothers are forced to sit on chairs all night, and you can't lie down next to the child in a small bed, and many spread a diaper on the tile and sleep like that. If the child is three years old, then the parents in the hospital are not fed, they cannot go out, there is only boiling water when the cook wants it, there are no outlets in the ward. The situation is the same in other departments, if there is a bath, it works until 20:00 in the evening, and then a lock is put on it. Medical sisters who should sit constantly on duty are forced to distribute food, not tablets. And the list can go on and on, we keep encountering this reality and it's just sad for RUSSIA, such a great power and such treatment of people! Why is it like this? How to solve ALL these problems without gagging us? How to give birth to children if no one considers themselves guilty when a child is born with disabilities, and everyone persuades you to refuse? HOW TO ACHIEVE JUSTICE????
